text: Eddard "Ned" Stark is a fictional character in the 1996 high fantasy novel A Game of Thrones by George R. R. Martin and in HBO's adaptation of the A Song of Ice and Fire series. He is the lord of Winterfell and warden of the North, the second son of Rickard Stark, and a lifelong friend of King Robert Baratheon, who invites Ned to become Hand of the King after the sudden death of their mentor, Jon Arryn. Ned is married to Lady Catelyn Tully and is the father of five trueborn children—Robb, Sansa, Arya, Bran, and Rickon—and has a bastard son, Jon Snow, as well as a ward, Theon Greyjoy. In the novel, Ned is portrayed as a virtuous, honorable patriarch with a strong moral compass, content to avoid courtly intrigue and committed to loyalty and honor. His family name, Stark, reflects both the resilience of his house and his resistance to moral compromise. Despite his principles, he is drawn into political corruption in King's Landing and ultimately faces a crisis between protecting his family and upholding his honor. He discovers that Robert's children with Cersei Lannister are the result of incest with her twin brother Jaime, and suspects Jon Arryn was poisoned to cover this truth. After being injured by Jaime Lannister and betrayed by Petyr "Littlefinger," Ned is imprisoned for treason. A secret deal with Varys leads him to publicly confess to treason in exchange for sparing his family, but King Joffrey orders his execution for amusement, forcing his daughter Sansa to view his severed head mounted on a spike. His execution shocks readers and viewers alike, as it subverts expectations of a heroic protagonist. In the follow-up novel A Clash of Kings, Ned's death ignites a civil war between House Stark and House Lannister, leading to the War of the Five Kings. His remains are returned to Catelyn, who sends them north to be laid in House Stark's ancestral crypt, though it is not confirmed whether they ever reach Winterfell due to the road being cut off by Ironborn invaders. Lady Barbrey Dustin claims she will never allow Ned's bones to be laid to rest in Winterfell. Ned is mentioned in flashbacks and referenced throughout later novels, including A Storm of Swords and A Dance with Dragons, where surviving Stark children, Stannis Baratheon, Jorah Mormont, and Northern mountain clans remember him with respect and affection. The mountain clans join Stannis' campaign to retake Winterfell in honor of Ned's legacy. In A Feast for Crows, Queen Cersei is haunted by visions of Ned silently mocking her. In the HBO adaptation, Sean Bean portrays Ned in the first season, with Sebastian Croft playing him as a child in season six and Robert Aramayo as a young adult in seasons six and seven. Bean was nominated for a Saturn Award and a Scream Award for the role and the cast was nominated for a Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by an Ensemble in a Drama Series in 2011. In the show, Ned is beheaded in the ninth episode, "Baelor," a move that shocked audiences and established a dramatic precedent that no one is safe. The producers, David Benioff and D. B. Weiss, stated that Ned's death was a key selling point for HBO, emphasizing the show's unpredictability and the idea that characters are not immune to danger. The image of Bean as Ned sitting in the Iron Throne appears on the covers of the 2011 Season 1 DVD and Blu-ray sets. Ned returns in season six through flashback visions seen by Bran and the Three-Eyed Raven. In the first season, Robert Baratheon visits Winterfell and asks Ned to become Hand of the King. Ned accepts to protect Robert and investigate Arryn's death, traveling to King's Landing with his daughters Arya and Sansa. Catelyn captures Tyrion Lannister, believing he orchestrated the assassination of Bran and the murder of Arryn. Ned and Robert disagree over Daenerys Targaryen, leading Ned to resign as Hand. After being attacked by Jaime Lannister, Ned is injured and his guards are killed. Robert reappoints him as Hand and orders Catelyn to release Tyrion. While Robert is hunting, Ned learns Tywin Lannister is besieging the Riverlands. He demands Tywin appear in King's Landing and sends forces to bring his bannermen to justice. Robert is killed during a boar hunt, and Ned is left to manage the kingdom. Before he can act against Cersei and place Stannis on the throne, he is betrayed by Littlefinger and imprisoned. Ned's eldest son, Robb, calls for action in response.

Catelyn has Tyrion Lannister captured, believing he was responsible for sending an assassin to kill Bran and that the Lannisters also killed Jon Arryn. Ned and Robert soon find themselves at odds regarding Daenerys Targaryen, and Ned steps down as Hand in defiance against Robert's wishes to have her killed. Soon after, Ned and his guards are attacked by Tyrion's brother Jaime Lannister; Ned is injured and his men are murdered. Robert reappoints Ned as Hand and commands him to have Catelyn release Tyrion and make peace with the Lannisters. While Robert departs for a boar hunt, Ned discovers that Tywin Lannister and his forces are laying siege to the Riverlands, the homeland of his wife's house, the Tullys. He demands Tywin present himself in King's Landing and sends a force to bring his bannermen to justice. Robert is killed just as Ned discovers that his three children by Cersei were actually fathered by the queen's twin, Jaime. Before Ned is able to neutralize Cersei and place Robert's brother Stannis on the throne, he is betrayed by Littlefinger, and the queen has him imprisoned for treason. Ned's eldest son Robb calls in his father's banners and marches an army south in an attempt to rescue his father. Ned makes a public confession to save his daughters from Cersei's wrath, but Joffrey has Ned beheaded anyway. In the season 6 episode "Home", Bran sees a vision of Ned (Sebastian Croft) as a child with his sister and brother, Lyanna and Benjen. In the following episode, "Oathbreaker", Bran witnesses the battle between a young Ned (Robert Aramayo) and the knight Ser Arthur Dayne at the Tower of Joy. In the episode "The Door", Bran watches Ned bid Benjen and his father, Rickard, farewell as he departs for his fosterage at the Vale. In the following episode, "Blood of My Blood", Bran briefly glimpses Ned's hand amongst someone's blood, revealed in the season finale, "The Winds of Winter", as belonging to Lyanna (Aisling Franciosi), dying of childbirth in the tower. She makes him swear to protect her son - Jon Snow. Bran revisits this moment in the season 7 finale, "The Dragon and the Wolf", where Lyanna whispers Jon's true name to Ned - Aegon Targaryen. Bean was nominated for a Saturn Award for Best Actor on Television, a Scream Award for Best Fantasy Actor, and an EWwy Award for Best Actor, Drama for the role. IGN named Ned its Best TV Hero of 2011, and Bean won the Portal Award for Best Actor.
